messages:
incident-bot: [AUTO] P1 alert — elevated error rate on tool/function invocation path and structured-output processing (hosted API, us-west). Trigger: tool-exec 5xx > 12% (5m). Link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/alerts/1123
Maya: paging oncall — @Oliver you're up for this window?
Oliver: Oncall here, looking at traces and queues now. I can see spikes in tool-exec latency and worker restarts.
Dmitri: I can repro high mem growth on the tool-sandbox process when structured JSON responses are enabled. Likely input explosion with unbounded tool results.
Oliver: Ok. We should immediately reduce blast radius. Mitigation options: rate-limit tool calls at the gateway, toggle structured-output enforcement to "degraded" or outright disable tool invocation for hosted tier. Quickest is a feature-flag toggle.
Maya: Agreed. Preference -> toggle tool invocations off for hosted customers, keep dedicated & private unchanged. That gives us space to stabilize without touching tenant configs. Sara, please start customer impact list (top 10 tenants using tool-calls).
Sara: On it. I'll message CSMs and open status page draft. Impact: any integrations relying on tool calls will now receive fallback: plain text responses + 503s for tool invocation attempts. We'll call out recommended client retry logic.
Oliver: I'll run the toggle. Patch to config service:

```bash
# disable external tool execution for hosted API (global toggle)
curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/v1/flags \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"flag":"enable_external_tools","value":false,"scope":"hosted"}'
```

Oliver: Applying now, will monitor error rate and latency.
deploy-bot: rollout initiated for flag enable_external_tools (target: hosted). rollout_id=ff-2026-03-15-1918
Dmitri: Seeing immediate drop in tool-exec queue length. Worker restarts down. Good signal.
Oliver: Error rate for clients that attempted tool calls is up (expected) but overall system 5xx for non-tool endpoints is down from 11% -> 3% in 4m.
Maya: Nice. Sara — publish the status update: brief description, mitigation, ETA for further updates. Use downtime window and list of impacted integrations.
Sara: Drafting now. Also pinging top 10 customers and setup dedicated support channel.
Oliver: Additional band-aid: Increasing per-tenant outbound throttling to 5r/s for tool endpoints in case we need to re-enable in limited capacity. Command:

```json
{"op":"patch","path":"/quotas/hosted/tool_calls","value":{"rate":5}}
```

Oliver: Not applying yet. Will hold until stability confirmed.
Ryan: I'm on deck in 20m, will take the handoff. For follow-ups: capture a few failing payload samples (redact PII) and a heap profile from tool-sandbox. Dmitri can you grab that?
Dmitri: Yep. Starting heap profile capture and will upload to the incident drive.
Maya: Handoff note: Oliver is primary until 12:30 UTC, then Ryan will take over. Make sure runbook steps for tool overload are followed: disable flag -> monitor -> quota patch -> customer comms.
Oliver: Adding a quick canary plan: once stable, test re-enabling for a small internal tenant with strict response size limits and structured-output turned to "parse-only" mode. If green for 10m, consider gradual rollout.
Sara: Status page posted, I tagged impacted customers and attached recommended client changes. Also added a line for support to use the channel #inc-1918002468 for updates.
deploy-bot: rollout completed (ff-2026-03-15-1918) — enable_external_tools=false for scope=hosted
Oliver: Monitoring continues. Will keep this channel updated. If error rate creeps up again we escalate to full traffic shaping (global token bucket) and consider short maintenance window.
Ryan: Taking over in 5. I have runbook open and will coordinate postmortem doc.
Maya: Thanks team — good rapid mitigation. Next steps: collect heap profiles, payload samples, postmortem draft, and a proposal for more granular per-tenant circuit breakers to avoid broad toggles next time.
Ryan: Acknowledged. I'll add follow-up tickets: (1) per-tenant tool-call quotas + auto-fallback, (2) structured-output parser hard-limits, (3) improved telemetry for tool execution size.
Dmitri: Uploading heap + sample payloads to the incident drive now -> https://drive.redwood.internal/incident/1918002468
Oliver: Closing active mitigation as of now — system metrics look stable. Keeping channel open for follow-up and postmortem.
Maya: Moving to monitoring state. Great work. :thumbsup:
